title: Five dead in Homagama factory fire - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - Five people have died following a fire that broke out at a helmet manufacturing factory in the Katuwana Industrial Zone in Homagama this morning (July 21).

The fire erupted at the factory located within the Katuwana Industrial Estate, and fire-fighting teams are continuing efforts to bring the blaze under control.

Further details regarding the identities of the deceased and the cause of the fire are yet to be confirmed.

title: No confidence motion on Justice Minister handed over to Speaker - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The Opposition handed over the no confidence motion on Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara to Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne today.

A group of Opposition MPs led by Chief Opposition Whip Gayantha Karunatilaka and Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) General Secretary Ranjith Madduma Bandara handed over the motion.

The main allegation against Minister Nanayakkara is his failure to prevent the recent clash at the Negombo prison.

title: Animals Amendment Bill presented to Parliament - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The Animals Amendment Bill which aims to amend the Animals Act, No. 29 of 1958, was presented to Parliament by the Minister of Agriculture and Livestock today.

The Bill comprises new regulations pertaining to animals.

title: Cattle meant for milking killed for meat: MP - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - Cattle meant for milking are killed for meat due to lack of grasslands, Opposition MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake alleged in Parliament today.

The MP said the Wildlife Department sues catte owners claiming that the cattle eat up grass meant for wild elephants and that the situation has created serious issues in areas such as the Maduru Oya forest reserve.

He said this has resulted in Sri Lanka spending billions for the import of milk powder.

Deputy Minister of Agriculture Namal Karunaratne, who responded, said the issue should be resolved with diligence through effective dialogue with all stakeholders.

title: At least 27 dead and 83 missing after passenger ferry capsizes off Guyana - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BBC - At least 27 people have drowned after a passenger ferry capsized off the coast of Guyana on Saturday night local time.

Sixty-nine people aboard the MV Barima had been rescued, Prime Minister Mark Phillips told reporters on Monday, adding 83 more remained missing.

Divers continue to search the site where the vessel capsized and people who believe their loved ones may have been on board the stricken vessel have been asked to contact the authorities.

"Our focus again is on finding people," said Phillips. "We still have hope."

An investigation into the tragedy had been launched, he said earlier.

"Let me be absolutely clear: where negligence, misconduct or criminal wrongdoing is established, those responsible will face the full force of the law," he said.

Guyana's Public Works Minister, Juan Edghill, expressed his anger at a news conference on Sunday, accusing those who operated the ferry of trying to "cheat the system".

The official registry had listed 133 as being on board the ferry, but Phillips said on Monday he was now "confident" there were 179 people.

Edghill also said the ferry's captain and at least one crew member had tested positive for cannabis.

"We have zero tolerance for members of the crew drinking or smoking while at work. And for us to have positive tests from the captain... this is serious," the minister said.

He added the captain and several of his crew had been taken into police custody.

The ferry, MV Barima, departed from the capital, Georgetown, on Saturday afternoon local time, headed for Port Kaituma, in the north of the country.

The 40m-long (131ft) vessel was built in 1939, according to a listing on VesselFinder.

A survivor, Elena Moonsammy, told local news site Kiskadee Watch that the ferry had tilted after being hit by a large wave, with water quickly rushing in.

It started to take on water within seconds, she said.

A distress call was received at 23:01 (03:01 GMT Sunday), triggering a search operation involving government teams and privately owned boats.

Moonsammy said she had survived by clinging to a box floating amidst the debris.

She had tried to hold on to the hand of her two-year-old child but they had been separated.

Moonsammy said she had managed to save a woman, whom she urged to also hold on to the floating box.

At least 15 children were among those rescued. Small private boats were key in pulling at least 17 survivors from the sea.

The French army sent 12 divers, two doctors and a mechanic from nearby French Guiana to aid the search-and-rescue operation.

Guyana's Health Minister, Dr Frank Anthony, said three of the survivors remained in hospital with minor injuries but the others had already been discharged.

Most, he added, had cuts and bruises from clinging to debris for hours.

title: National Environmental Act comes into force from today - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) Speaker Dr. Jagath Wickramaratne today endorsed the certificate for the National Environmental (Amendment) Bill, which was passed by Parliament.

The Act is intended to further strengthen the legal framework for the protection, management, and enhancement of the environment, improve regulatory mechanisms relating to waste disposal, and modernize the mechanisms used for environmental protection.

Accordingly, the Bill comes into force as the National Environmental (Amendment) Act, No. 15 of 2026.

title: Flash floods kill at least 20 in Afghanistan and leave more than 100 missing - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
abc NEWS - Flash floods in eastern Afghanistan have killed 20 people, injured about 80 more and left more than 100 missing, Afghan authorities said Monday.

The floods struck the eastern province of Nuristan, said Yousaf Hammad, spokesman for the Afghanistan National Disaster Management Authority, adding that a search and rescue operation was underway to locate the missing.

“Unfortunately, severe floods today in Parun city and several other areas of Nuristan province have caused heavy loss of life and property among our fellow citizens,” Hammad said, adding that the floods had caused extensive damage to people’s homes, agricultural land and public facilities.

“We urge all citizens to stay away from flood-prone areas and zones at risk,” he said.

Afghanistan is highly vulnerable to extreme weather events, with snow and heavy rain that trigger flash floods, often killing dozens, or even hundreds, of people at a time. In 2024, more than 300 people died in springtime flash floods. Earlier this year, at least 110 people were killed by widespread flooding and landslides in several parts of the country

Decades of conflict, along with poor infrastructure, a struggling economy, deforestation and the intensifying effects of climate change, have amplified the impact of such disasters, particularly in remote areas where many homes are built of mud and offer limited protection against sudden deluges or heavy snowfall.

“We were saddened to learn that floods caused loss of life and property damage in Nuristan province this afternoon,” said government spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid. “We pray for those who lost their lives in this incident and for a speedy recovery for the injured.”

More extreme weather was forecast, with heavy rain, thunderstorms, strong winds accompanied by dust and sand, and flash floods predicted for 10 of the country’s 34 provinces, the Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation’s meteorology department said. The ministry warned residents to avoid riverbanks and other areas at risk of flooding.

title: Detention fees force importers to abandon luxury cars - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - Around 1,000 imported luxury vehicles are being abandoned at the Hambantota Port because importers cannot afford the high detention fees charged to release them, Sri Lanka Customs officials said.

He said nearly 40,000 imported vehicles are currently parked at the port. Many have remained there due to disruptions in re-export operations and the conflict in the Middle East, which has affected shipping to destinations such as Dubai. Vehicles brought in for re-export are also facing the same detention fee problem.

The Customs official said a local importer recently tried to release a luxury vehicle worth about Rs. 20 million that had been parked at the port for nearly six years. However, he was told he had to pay almost Rs. 50 million in detention charges.

This increased the total cost of the vehicle to nearly Rs. 70 million, more than three times its original value.

The official said the importer decided not to release the vehicle after learning about the charges.

Official said many importers are making similar decisions, leaving hundreds of luxury vehicles abandoned at the port as detention fees continue to rise.

title: Fire breaks out at helmet factory in Homagama - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - A fire broke out at a helmet manufacturing factory in the Katuwana Industrial Estate in Homagama this morning, the Homagama Headquarters Police said.

According to residents, thick black smoke from the blaze spread across the surrounding area, reducing visibility and causing concern among nearby communities.

Police said the fire was continuing to spread at the time of reporting.

The Kotte Municipal Council Fire Brigade has been called in to bring the fire under control. No casualties or the cause of the fire have been reported so far.

title: Rice imports hit local production by 60%, says National Agrarians’ Unity - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Mangala Pavithrani

Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The import of nearly 100,000 metric tons of rice has severely disrupted the local rice market, reducing demand for domestically produced rice by around 60% and creating a crisis for farmers ahead of the 2026 Yala harvesting season, National Agrarians' Unity Chairman Anuradha Tennakoon claimed.

Addressing a media briefing, Tennakoon alleged that the volume of imported rice far exceeded the country's actual requirement, leaving warehouses belonging to small, medium and large-scale rice mill owners filled with unsold stocks.

He warned that the situation could significantly affect paddy purchases during the upcoming Yala season, placing thousands of farmers at risk.

Tennakoon said the expected paddy harvest for the 2026 Yala season is around 1.8 million metric tons. In addition, he claimed that farmers are still holding between 500,000 and 700,000 metric tons of unsold paddy from the 2025/26 Maha season, representing about 35% of the total Maha harvest.

He said the country's total paddy stock could increase to between 2.4 million and 2.5 million metric tons with the Yala harvest, while demand for locally produced rice and paddy has fallen sharply due to imports.

Tennakoon also alleged that the Paddy Marketing Board (PMB) has restricted paddy purchases to between 2,000 and 2,500 kilograms per farmer in major farming districts, including Ampara.

He said farmers cultivating between two and five acres typically produce between 5,000 and 6,000 kilograms of paddy, leaving a substantial portion of their harvest unsold under the current purchasing limits.

Questioning how farmers were expected to manage the excess stocks, Tennakoon asked whether the remaining paddy should be stored "in the homes of agricultural officers or ministers."

He further criticised new PMB guidelines requiring each paddy bag to weigh exactly 50.250 kilograms, describing the requirement as impractical and alleging that it was intended to slow the government's purchasing process and discourage farmers from selling their harvest.

Tennakoon also claimed that taxes imposed on fertiliser, agrochemicals and agricultural equipment had further increased production costs, adding to the financial difficulties faced by farmers.

title: Applications open for Second Efficiency Bar Examination for teachers - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The Examinations Department has called for applications for the Second Efficiency Bar Examination for Sri Lanka Teachers' Service officers serving in national and provincial schools, scheduled to be held in September 2026.

The relevant Gazette notification was published on July 17, 2026, while online applications will be accepted from July 20 to August 10 through the official website of the Examinations Department.

According to the notification, teachers who were directly recruited to Grade 2-II of the Sri Lanka Teachers' Service based on a Bachelor of Education (B.Ed.) degree, as well as those promoted or appointed to Grade 2-II after initially being recruited to Grade 3, are required to complete the II Efficiency Bar Examination before completing four years of service in Grade 2-II.

In addition, teachers who had not completed the Second Efficiency Bar Examination before June 30, 2025, but were promoted to Grade 2-I subject to fulfilling that requirement, must pass the examination to qualify for further promotion to Grade 1 of the Sri Lanka Teachers' Service.

The Department said the syllabus for the self-study modules related to the examination has been published on the e-Thaksalawa website of the Ministry of Education, as stated in the Gazette notification.

Candidates have been encouraged to prepare for the examination through self-study by accessing the learning materials available on the e-Thaksalawa platform before sitting the examination in September.

title: Health services face uncertainty over circular on acting specialist doctors - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - A circular issued by the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIM) has sparked concern over the functioning of specialist medical services, with a doctors' trade union warning that it could disrupt healthcare delivery across the country.

The circular, issued by the Senior Registrar of the PGIM on June 26 to all Directorates of Studies, states that acting specialist doctors who have completed their specialist medical training but have not yet obtained the PGIM Board Certificate should not independently examine patients, make clinical decisions, or issue medical recommendations within their specialty.

Doctors' Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights Chairman and Specialist Dr Chamal Sanjeewa said the directive has created a serious challenge, as many hospitals are already facing a shortage of specialist doctors.

He said the Health Ministry currently deploys doctors who have completed their local postgraduate specialist training as acting specialists to base hospitals and specialist units across the country to address staffing shortages.

According to Dr Sanjeewa, the new instructions make it difficult for these acting specialists to function independently, potentially affecting the delivery of specialist healthcare services.

He urged the Health Ministry Secretary to immediately issue clear guidelines to all specialist and acting specialist doctors on how the circular should be implemented to avoid disruptions to patient care.

Dr Sanjeewa also questioned the timing of the directive, noting that many specialist units in hospitals across the island are currently being managed by acting specialist doctors who have not yet completed their overseas training but continue to provide essential services.

He further said that many acting specialist doctors also engage in private practice in the areas where they serve. If they are not legally permitted to independently examine patients or make medical recommendations under the new circular, the legal status of those private medical services also becomes unclear.

Dr Sanjeewa called on the Health Secretary to clarify the matter publicly to ensure patient safety and maintain public confidence in the country's healthcare system.

title: Rs 26.2 million spent for Rohana Wijeweera’s family - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - Public funds of Rs. 26,278,052 has been spent for the late founder of the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP) Rohana Wijeweera's family since his demise, it has been revealed.

The answer given by the government to a question raised by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera has revealed that the Sri Lankan government has originally spent the said amount to support Chithrangani Wijeweera and six children.

However the government currently supports Ms. Wijeweera and her eldest daughter with special needs.

title: Father seeks probe into daughter’s death at Ratnapura Hospital - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 21 (Daily Mirror) - The father of a 21-year-old girl who died while receiving treatment at the General Hospital in Ratnapura has called on the Health Ministry to launch an immediate and independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding her death, alleging possible medical negligence.

In a letter addressed to the Health Minister, the father requested a ministerial inquiry into the death of his daughter, who died after being admitted to Ward 13 of the General Hospital, Ratnapura.

According to the letter, she was admitted through the hospital’s Emergency Treatment Unit (ETU) on July 3 after being diagnosed with pneumonia and was later transferred to Ward 13.

The father alleged that despite repeated requests by family members, his daughter was not adequately reviewed by the treating consultant, medical officers or nursing staff. He further claimed that her complaints of severe chest pain, bleeding from the mouth, persistent diarrhoea and worsening shortness of breath were not acted upon appropriately.

He also alleged that her oxygen saturation level had dropped to 85 per cent on the day of admission and, although oxygen therapy was administered, the treating consultant was not informed promptly, and no urgent escalation of care was initiated.

According to the complaint, the patient’s condition continued to deteriorate until she suffered a cardiac arrest in the ward. She was subsequently transferred to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), where she later died.

Furthermore, father said the Judicial Medical Officer (JMO) had indicated that the provisional cause of death was pneumonia, pending histopathological examination.

As such, he requested the Health Ministry to appoint an independent investigation team to review the patient’s medical records, nursing notes, observation charts, medication records and investigation results, examine whether proper monitoring and escalation procedures had been followed, obtain statements from the medical and nursing staff involved, and determine whether accepted standards of medical care had been maintained.

Meanwhile, speaking to the Daily Mirror, Ratnapura Teaching Hospital Director Dr A.D.H. Jayathilake confirmed that the hospital had received the letter regarding the incident.

Dr Jayathilake said the hospital is currently gathering information related to the matter and that the circumstances surrounding the incident are being investigated.

He added that further details would be available once the inquiry is completed.
